transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and my neck. It’s like, every time I look in the mirror, that’s all I see. And people tell me it looks normal, you know, like my sister will say, “You’re fine,” but I don’t believe it.

I work around families and nurses, and I go to church, and I just feel like when people look at me, that’s the first thing they notice. Even if they’re talking about something completely different, I’m sitting there thinking they’re staring at my neck. It’s been really bothering me.
How much time do you spend each day thinking about the way your jaw and neck look?

A lot… I mean, I don’t know exactly in hours, but it feels like it keeps coming back all day. I’ll catch myself thinking about that sagging uneven place around my jaw and neck, even when I’m supposed to be focused on work.

Like when I’m with families or around the nurses, or even at church, I’m wondering if they’re noticing it. People say it looks normal, but I just can’t stop seeing it.
Have you ever considered that others might not notice this sagging because it’s actually not as visible as it seems to you?

I mean… I’ve tried to tell myself that, that maybe they don’t notice it the way I do. But then I’ll be talking to a family at work, or one of the nurses, and my mind goes right back to my jaw and neck. Like that sagging, uneven spot is just sitting there, and I feel like it’s the first thing they see.

Even at church, when people are just being friendly, I’ll think, are they looking at it? Folks tell me it looks normal, but I can’t really take that in. I just keep seeing it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to cover up the area, or comparing your jaw and neck to other people, because of how you feel about their appearance?

Yes… I do. Mostly before I leave for work, or if I have some meeting or something at church, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I’ll fix my collar, then move my hair around my neck, then look again like maybe I can make it sit right.

And then I’ll get my phone out and check the camera too, which is silly because the lighting in there is awful anyway—my daughter’s always telling me that bathroom makes everybody look bad. But I still do it. Sometimes I ask her, “Does this look strange?” and she’ll say no, but I’ll ask again or keep fussing with it.

It’s made me late more than once, because I’ll think I’m ready and then I go back and check it one more time.
Have you ever avoided going to work, church, or spending time with people because you were too worried about how your jaw or neck looked?

Yes… not usually calling out of work completely, but I’ve avoided parts of it. Like, I’ve passed up helping lead meetings or taking on more of the supervisor-type responsibilities, because I just picture everyone looking at my face and neck while I’m talking.

And then sometimes I get so stuck trying to look presentable before work that I fall behind on paperwork later, which is embarrassing because I’m usually pretty responsible with that.

Church… I still go some, but I’ve skipped things. And I used to do book club and walking club more, but lately I’ll think about getting ready and what I’ll look like, and it just feels like too much. Then I stay home, and I tell myself I was tired or busy, but really it’s that.
